checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: Brier/log-loss/reliability calibration and SelfModel scoring (research-engine transfer)

impact_assessment.why: Brain's SelfModel records confidence and outcomes but never scores whether the confidence is calibrated. research-engine/engine/calibration.py:38-159 provides Brier, log loss, base rate, skill, reliability bins and small-sample warnings.
impact_assessment.benefits: A pure calibration.summary over forecasts returns counts/coverage/Brier/log loss/skill/bins/warnings; SelfModel.calibration() scores the recorded confidence/outcome pairs; perfect/inverted fixtures discriminate; behavior is unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new calibration.py and SelfModel.calibration; dependency: stdlib math only; concurrency: none; state: outcomes list additive, snapshot unchanged.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use proper scoring rules with probability clipping, validate inputs, ignore unresolved outcomes, warn below the minimum, and test perfect/calibrated/inverted/empty/coverage fixtures plus a real T3 run; full gates.

[1/4] Plan: immutable claim/verdict records with kill tests and a ledger (research-engine transfer)

impact_assessment.why: Brain has calibration and snapshot evidence but no structured claim with a kill test, verdict status or verdict history. research-engine/engine/claims.py and verdict records provide claim status, confidence, kill tests and supports/refutes/inconclusive evidence.
impact_assessment.benefits: Claims carry id/text/kill_test/confidence/status; record_verdict preserves history and maps supports/refutes/inconclusive; the ledger summarizes counts; to_dict/from_dict roundtrips; T3 claims can be judged from run outcomes without changing actions.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claims.py; dependency: stdlib dataclasses only; concurrency: none; state: in-memory records only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate ids/text/kill tests/confidence/status; make claims immutable so history cannot be rewritten; test transitions, invalid inputs, summary, roundtrip and real T3 claims; full gates.

[1/4] Plan: single-target BFS backend progress guard for legal wrong-way moves

impact_assessment.why: The no-op guard rejects wait/premature collect/blocked movement, but a legal free-cell move away from a fixed target is accepted until the 20-step trust window expires: T3:15 costs 33 steps/21 calls instead of 13/13, T3:65 26 instead of 6, T2:3 34 instead of 8.
impact_assessment.benefits: A backend movement that strictly increases BFS distance to the fixed target is rejected immediately with reason no-progress; T3:15 33->13, T3:65 26->6, T2:3 34->8, calls 21->13/6/8; T1 item tours and no-target states stay 36/22.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Planner progress_guard keyword and PLANNER_POLICY key (policy digest changes); dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Apply only when a fixed target exists and no items remain; compare against the rule action's BFS distance; keep progress_guard opt-out; preserve T1 and rule-only behavior; test equal-distance acceptance, invalid flags, and run the full suite plus AIKit.

[1/4] Plan: append-only hash-chained Merkle batch journal with historical proofs

impact_assessment.why: The single .merkle sidecar is overwritten by each new anchor, so an earlier batch root and its inclusion proofs are lost. The telemetry anchor journal solved the same overwrite problem for head anchors.
impact_assessment.benefits: append_merkle_anchor appends batches with prev/hash links and monotonic ranges; verify_merkle_journal names prev/order/root/truncation defects; merkle_proof_for_journal_record proves membership in an earlier batch after a newer anchor is written; the single-anchor API is unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new journal functions/wrappers; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: single-writer append under fsync (same boundary as the single anchor); state: new .merkle.journal sidecar, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the single-anchor format untouched; validate every record's schema/ranges/root/prev/hash; reject range rollback; test intact, truncated, deleted, tampered, rollback, missing and proof cases; run 266 tests and AIKit.
